observations: The two headings and their operative prescriptions distinguish 3.2.110 luṅ from 3.2.111 laṅ. The latter also preserves a separate Vārttika with laṅ. The examples a-karot and a-harat belong below the 3.2.111 prescription.

The third-edition title leaf identifies Śobhita Miśra and 1952. Its p. 187 prints luṅ at 3.2.110 and laṅ at 3.2.111 in both headings and operative glosses, with the same imperfect examples and a separately stated Vārttika.
The 3.1.34 text gives patāti at the no-siP control. Note 5 assigns padāti and the root pad gatau to the Nyāsa reading.
decisions: Accept laṅ as the 3.2.111 operative prescription in both editions. Record the received Git-child luṅ as a documentary divergence for this field, excluded from the PG348 operational branch. The genuine 3.2.110 luṅ and separately addressed Vārttika keep their own scopes. The editor's motive and both transmission lineages remain Open.

Accept patāti at the main-text address and padāti at the editorial-report address. The latter corroborates PG704's source-specific distinction and leaves direct Vedic attestation for the d-root control Open.
edition_readings: Accepted as this edition's direct main reading
